text:
maria: I want to float an idea — a bandwidth-aware offload scheduler for host<->GPU transfers.
maria: Instead of evict/keep purely by hotness, we weight decisions by expected PCIe/host bandwidth impact so small-latency requests don't get wedged behind huge bulk transfers.
jun: sounds useful for interactive workloads. how do you see this fitting with current eviction + prefetch hints?
sashank: main concern: tenant fairness. if we prioritize tiny transfers for one tenant, others could be starved for throughput. need quota/gating.
maria: yeah — think of two levers: (1) urgency buckets (interactive/normal/batch) and (2) bandwidth budget windows per tenant/pool. scheduler enforces both.
olivia: API boundary question: is this a runtime-level transfer scheduler or allocator hints that allocator/runtime coordinate on?
maria: proposer: runtime implements scheduler, allocator emits hints (urgency, estimated_bytes, can_prefetch). runtime makes final decision based on topology and current inflight bandwidth.
alex: simpler incremental approach: implement tenant-level bandwidth gates + an urgency flag. no complex hotness reweighting yet. gives most benefit with low implementation cost. :+1:
jun: telemetry needed: pcie_bytes_inflight, transfers_queued_by_urgency, avg_transfer_size, p99_latency_by_urgency. without that we can't tune windows.
sashank: other tradeoffs: packing/coalescing transfers optimizes throughput but increases tail latency for urgent transfers. scheduler needs to avoid coalescing urgent items.
maria: draft API sketch:

```
// Alloc hint emitted at allocation time
struct AllocHint {\n  string urgency; // "interactive" | "normal" | "batch"\n  uint64 estimated_bytes;\n  bool allow_prefetch;\n}

// runtime config
bandwidth_windows: {\n  tenant_id: {window_bytes: 200000000, refill_ms: 1000} // simple token-bucket per tenant\n}
```

olivia: test plan: microbench with mixed traffic: seq_len=64 interactive mix (40%) + seq_len=2048 batch (60%), sweep bandwidth windows and measure 95/99 latency. I can prototype.
jun: perf runner command example: `./perf.sh --profile offload-sched --pattern mixed --iters 5000`
sashank: topology note: PCIe lanes and NUMA matter. a transfer that crosses CPU NUMA nodes can eat more host latency. scheduler should be topo-aware (read /sys/class/pci or use hwloc).
maria: agreed — runtime should annotate bandwidth cost with topology multiplier.
alex: also watch for alignment with batching: kernel selection expects certain batch sizes; if we preempt big transfers too aggressively we could waste kernel efficiency. need cost model that includes compute vs transfer tradeoff.
maria: OK next steps: olivia protos microbench + jun hooks up telemetry, sashank explores topology probe, alex owns a minimal gate POC. I'll draft a short RFC next week.
olivia: I'll grab the prototype, aiming for a ~2-day spike.
sashank: noted. will paste a quick sysfs helper in the RFC.
deploy-bot: canary pipeline triggered for infra-experiments/offload-sched-probe (no-prod).
maria: thanks all — please drop short bullets in the RFC PR so I can synthesize. :rocket:
